stories.title: Bitcoin dips below $59,000 as Asian chip stocks slide and bitcoin funds lose money for a sixth day
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $59,000 late Tuesday US time as a sell-off in technology and chip shares spread from Wall Street to Asia. US spot bitcoin funds have now lost money six days in a row.
points: Bitcoin was about $59,062 at 1am ET Wednesday, down 2.2% in 24 hours, after touching about $58,924 late Tuesday, per The Block.
US spot bitcoin funds lost $231.6 million on Tuesday 24 Nov, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $175.3 million, per SoSoValue data reported by TokenPost.
That follows a $570 million outflow on Monday, which took November's total to nearly $5 billion, per The Block.
South Korea's Kospi lost 6.2% and Japan's Nikkei 2.8%, after the Nasdaq fell 1.5% on Tuesday, per AP.
US spot ether funds lost $64 million on Tuesday, per The Block.

stories.title: Today's US inflation report is the last big one before the Fed's December decision
stories.summary: October's PCE inflation report, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, comes out at 8:30am ET today (20:30 Bangkok) together with the second estimate of third-quarter growth. Markets already expect the Fed to raise rates on 9 December.
points: PCE is expected to rise 0.3% on the month after 0.5% in September, per ActionForex.
Forecasts for core PCE over the year differ: 3.2% (ActionForex) or 3.4% (ZeroHedge); September was 3.1%.
Q3 growth is expected at 3.5%, up from the first estimate of 3.4%, per ActionForex.
CME FedWatch showed about a 97% chance of a rate hike in December, per Reuters as reported by FXEmpire on 25 Nov.
Jobless claims, durable goods orders and new home sales are also out today, per The Block, and the Fed's Beige Book follows at 2:00pm ET, per ZeroHedge.

stories.title: US moves to seize more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen in the Binance hack
stories.summary: The US Justice Department has filed a court case to take over more than $1.1 billion of USDC stablecoins it links to North Korean hackers who robbed Binance in October. Circle, which issues USDC, froze the coins soon after the hack.
points: The civil forfeiture complaint was filed on Monday 23 Nov in federal court in Washington, DC, and covers USDC at 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, per Bitcoin Magazine.
The Justice Department says more than $6 billion was stolen in the 29 Oct hack and blames North Korea's Lazarus Group, per Bitcoin Magazine.
Circle will issue replacement USDC to the US government if a court orders the forfeiture, per Bitcoin Magazine.
The attack began with a fake job recruiter who got an employee to install malware, per Fox Business.

briefs.title: New US tariffs on 16 trading partners still not announced
briefs.summary: The US is still preparing to unveil new tariffs on 16 trading partners, with no date or rates given yet, per the BBC via Yahoo News.

briefs.title: Strategy buys 457 more bitcoin
briefs.summary: Strategy paid $29.6 million for 457 bitcoin and now holds 851,305, at an average cost of $75,446 each, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: CFTC staff let bitcoin and ether count toward derivatives firms' expense buffers
briefs.summary: Bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins can now count, with a haircut, toward the money derivatives exchanges and clearing houses must hold to cover a year of operating costs, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kalshi pauses in Utah
briefs.summary: Prediction market Kalshi paused for more than 177,000 Utah users while a court rules on the CFTC's case against the state; a New York judge refused to shut it down there, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kraken plans two US credit cards for early 2027
briefs.summary: Kraken's Krak app opened a waitlist for two cards with up to 4% cashback in dollars or bitcoin, per The Block.

briefs.title: Moscow Exchange to start crypto trading on 1 December
briefs.summary: Russia's main exchange will list bitcoin, ether and USDT, with retail buyers capped at 300,000 rubles a year per broker, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: South Korea publishes its draft digital-asset law
briefs.summary: The draft allows bank-led won stablecoins, caps exchange shareholders at 20% and makes exchanges liable for hack losses, per The Block.

briefs.title: Ethereum Foundation doubles its security team
briefs.summary: The foundation says AI is a more urgent risk than quantum computing, per The Block.
